body.statement: If \(r_n(T_n-\theta)\) converges in distribution to \(T\), \(r_n\to\infty\), and \(g\) is differentiable at \(\theta\), then \(r_n\{g(T_n)-g(\theta)\}\) converges in distribution to \(Dg(\theta)T\).

source.verbatim_statement: Let phi be a map defined on a subset of R^k and differentiable at theta. Let T_n be random vectors such that r_n(T_n-theta) converges in distribution to T for numbers r_n tending to infinity. Then r_n(phi(T_n)-phi(theta)) converges in distribution to phi'_theta(T).

attestation.note: Transcribed from van der Vaart, Asymptotic Statistics (Cambridge University Press, 1998), Theorem 3.1; publisher source consulted.
